    RELATED LAWS & CODES: AC 28-113, BC 1604.1, BC 1708.2

 I. BACKGROUND
    Buildings, structures, and parts thereof must be designed and constructed in accordance with strength
    design, load and resistance factor design, allowable stress design, empirical design, or conventional
    construction methods, as outlined in Building Code, Section 1604.1. This bulletin specifically establishes
    criteria to determine the load profile of Adhesive-Based Solar Pedestal Bonding Systems to be used with BC
    1604.1.


 II. DESCRIPTION
    An Adhesive-Based Solar Pedestal Bonding System is an alternative option for installing solar panels to
    roofs. Unlike conventional methods that require drilling holes and welding, which can potentially damage the
    roof, the Adhesive-Based Solar Pedestal Bonding System uses a structural adhesive to bond solar mounts
    to the roof surface. Solar photovoltaic panels will then be secured to the mounts.


 III. USES
    Adhesive-Based Solar Pedestal Bonding Systems support and secure solar panel mounts to roofing
    assemblies.


 IV. EVALUATION SCOPE
    NYC Construction Codes


 V. EVALUATION CRITERIA
    Pursuant to AC 28-113, the Office of Technical Certification and Research (OTCR) recognizes Adhesive-
    Based Solar Pedestal Bonding Systems when evaluated and designed in accordance with New York City
    Building Code Section 1708.2:
    1708.2 Test standards. Structural components and assemblies shall be tested in accordance with the
    appropriate material standards listed in Chapter 35. In the absence of a standard that contains an applicable
    load test procedure, the test procedure shall be developed by a registered design professional and approved.

     The test procedure shall simulate loads and conditions of application that the completed structure or portion
     thereof will be subjected to in normal use.
     Until such a standard is created and adopted by DOB that contains applicable load procedures, the following
     shall be required:
     •   A registered design professional must establish a test procedure based on TAS 114-95, Test Procedures
         for Roofing Assemblies in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone Jurisdiction, Appendix D Test Procedure for
         Simulated Uplift Pressure Resistance of Adhered Roofing Assemblies. Testing Application Standards
         (TAS) were developed for use in the High Velocity Hurricane Zone of Florida. TAS protocols are found in
         the test protocols section of the Florida Building code. OTCR has determined that the TAS should be
         used as the basis for an acceptable testing program.
     •   A modified TESTING APPLICATION STANDARD (TAS) 114-95, Appendix D must be used. Modifications
         to this standard are necessary as the unmodified standard is tailored to test static uplift resistance of
         roofing membranes. The standard requires adjustments to assess the strength of the recommended
         adhesives used to secure the mounting pedestal to the top of the roofing membrane. The standard should
         be revised to accommodate attachment of roof-mounted solar panels.
     •   Testing performed in accordance with the modified TESTING APPLICATION STANDARD (TAS) 114-95,
         Appendix D will be accepted. Considerations should be given to sections 7.2 and 7.4, other sections at
         the discretion of the registered design professional, and ASCE 7. Testing and use of the adhesive-based
         solar pedestal bonding system shall include specific conditions for the intended use. A qualified registered
         design professional must have 3 years of relevant experience in load testing.


   VI. CONDITIONS OF ACCEPTANCE
     Adhesive-based Solar Pedestal Bonding Systems shall comply with the NYC Construction Codes and the
     following applicable provisions:
     A. Filing. A testing report based on the modified TAS 114-95 Appendix D shall be submitted as a
        construction document. The report shall document testing representative of the proposed on-site
        installation conditions and be available to support required inspections.

     B. Design. Adhesive-based Solar Pedestal Bonding Systems shall be designed in accordance with the NYC
        Construction Codes, the conditions of the modified TAS 114-95 test, and the conditions of this Bulletin.
         The design applicant must verify that the field conditions are consistent with the tested conditions to
         ensure compliance and proper performance.

     C. Installation Requirements. Installation requirements shall be in accordance with the NYC Construction
        Codes, manufacturer’s installation instructions, the results of the modified TAS test report, and the
        conditions of this Bulletin.

     D. Inspections. Pursuant to section BC 1705.1.1, the installation of Adhesive-Based Solar Pedestal
        Bonding Systems shall be subject to special inspection requirements of Chapter 17 of the Building Code
        and Department Rules covering special inspection.
         The design applicant is responsible for the following in DOB NOW:
         a) Identify Adhesive-Based Solar Pedestal Bonding Systems as a required special inspection.
         b) Certify that the special inspection agency engaged by the owner to supervise the Adhesive-Based
            Solar Pedestal Bonding Systems inspection is acceptable.

         Special Inspectors of Adhesive-Based Solar Pedestal Bonding Systems shall:
         a) Maintain the same qualification requirements for the Structural - Stability – Alterations to Existing
            Structures, Construction Operations Influencing Adjacent Structures, Mechanical Means and
            Methods of Demolition, Other Means of Demolition, and Raising and Moving of a Building category
            as defined in 1 RCNY §101-06, Appendix A.
         b) Have duties and responsibilities in accordance with but not limited to 1RCNY §101-06 and BC
            §1704.1.1.2. The inspector shall verify that the field conditions are acceptable based on the
            requirements set by the design applicant, the conditions tested for in the submitted TAS test report, the
            approved drawings, and the conditions established in this Bulletin (see Section VI. A of this Bulletin).
            As part of such duties, the special inspection agency shall examine all approved construction
            documents relating to the work subject to special inspection to confirm that the documents are
            sufficient to enable proper performance of the inspection, and shall confirm that any shop drawings,
            submittals, or sketches have been accepted in writing by the registered design professional of record.
            All approved construction documents shall be maintained on site and be accessible to the special
            inspector at the time of inspection.; and
         c) Identify the responsibility for the special inspection of Adhesive-Based Solar Pedestal Bonding
            Systems and certify the completeness of all required inspection and testing activities in DOB NOW.
